newsitem.title: USA: US Q3 mortgage delinquencies down to 4.16 pct--MBA.
newsitem.headline: US Q3 mortgage delinquencies down to 4.16 pct--MBA.

text.p: U.S. mortgage delinquencies fell in the third quarter of 1996, marking the third straight quarterly decline, according to a survey by the Mortgage Bankers Association of America.

The overall seasonally adjusted delinquency rate for one- to four-unit homes was 4.16 percent in the third quarter, down from 4.35 percent in the previous quarter, the group said. "A healthy economy has generated strong job and income gains, making it easier for consumers to meet their monthly mortgage obligations," MBA President Ron McCord said.
McCord said low interest rates have also been a factor in the improved delinquency situation, which he predicted would remain "in a steady holding pattern" in the near future.

He told reporters that "interest rates in all likelihood will remain somewhat stable" next year, noting signs of an economic slowdown in recent weeks. But he said the group has not revised its earlier forecast for higher interest rates in 1997.
The Northeast region's delinquency rate showed the most improvement, ending the third quarter 25 basis points lower at 4.24 percent.

In the South, the delinquency rate was down 22 basis points to 4.84 percent. The rate fell 20 basis points to 3.40 percent in the West and 18 basis points to 3.83 percent in the Nort Central region, the MBA said.
The delinquency rate continued to improve in all categories. It has reached levels not seen since 1980 for loans that are past due for 90 days or more.

Nationally, foreclosure data were mixed. The percentage of foreclosures started in the quarter fell one basis point to 0.33 percent, while the percentage of loans in foreclosure at the quarter's end rose 4 basis points to 1.00 percent.

The mortgage bankers' group noted that the overall third quarter decline in delinquencies was greater than in the previous two quarters, confirming that the rate "has turned a corner from its cyclical peak in the fourth quarter of 1995."
At the same time, however, consumer debt levels are approaching historic highs, while the servicing of that debt as a percentage of disposable income is also rising, the MBA said.
As a result, only modest improvements in delinquency rates are expected in the next several quarters, the group said in its report.
